# The current account

*What the record now holds about how its own argument fits together, one
line at a time. Generated from the SYNTHESIS entries in
`record/syntheses.d/`: edit those, not this page.*

A synthesis is an account of a scope of the record's argument, a line or a
part of one. It names every component, attributes each link between them to
the entry that states it, and adds nothing of its own. A claim that adds to
its components is a CLAIM, and appears here as one of the components. The
status beside each component, with its kind, is read from the component
when this page is built, so a component retired since the account was
written shows as retired here. An `Open` QUESTION, an `Active` TERM and a
`Proposed` CLAIM are different kinds of standing, which is why the kind is
shown. An account marked *Current* has had its mapping reviewed by the
owner. One marked *Proposed* is offered and not yet reviewed. Neither status
says anything about the components, which keep their own. An account that
spans several lines is set out under its first and pointed to from the
others. An account built over the accounts of its parts is set out once,
with each part account nested under it in place of a row in its table, so
every account appears here once.

## Will-organization

what organizes practical efficacy in an agent, and how that organization becomes precarious. Normative judgment about organizations is a line of its own ([ADR-089](../record/decisions.d/ADR-089.md))

### [SYNTHESIS-035](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-035.md): The will-organization line is five accounts that meet at its central thesis, that maintained relations of efficacy decide which of an agent's regimes becomes effective: what decides it, how a population of interests acts as one, frustration among demands, maintaining the capacity to govern, and freedom of will and self-formation; the line makes no claim beyond its parts, one of them is mostly closed, and normative judgment about organizations, once a sixth part, is a line of its own

*Proposed · version 2*

The account of the will-organization line, over the accounts of its five parts: which regime becomes effective ([SYNTHESIS-036](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-036.md)), acting as one ([SYNTHESIS-037](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-037.md)), frustration and thresholds ([SYNTHESIS-044](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-044.md)), maintaining the capacity to govern ([SYNTHESIS-039](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-039.md)), and freedom of will and self-formation ([SYNTHESIS-041](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-041.md)). They meet at [CLAIM-027](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md) and [CLAIM-025](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md), on which claims of four parts rest, and at [CLAIM-354](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md), [CLAIM-523](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) and [CLAIM-445](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-445.md). No link between the parts that the record does not state passed [ADR-075](../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s test, so the account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'. Normative judgment about organizations, version 1's sixth part, is the line organizational-normativity ([ADR-089](../record/decisions.d/ADR-089.md)), with its own account ([SYNTHESIS-038](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md)).

#### [SYNTHESIS-036](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-036.md): Which of an agent's available regimes becomes effective is decided by maintained relations of efficacy that are not further preferences and are indexed to an agent rather than to any regulator; precedence, jurisdiction and suspension among them vary separately; and whether describing them as one organization explains anything that the fields studying each realizer do not is open

*Proposed · version 2*

A part account of the will-organization line: the will paper's central thesis and what the record holds about it. Which regime becomes effective depends on maintained relations that are not the competing regimes' contents ([CLAIM-027](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md), Active), resting on possession not being efficacy ([CLAIM-047](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-047.md)) and on a supposed agent ([CLAIM-080](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-080.md)). Its objections are answered or held: the permissiveness objection by agent-indexing, the redescription objection by [CLAIM-122](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-122.md) and [CLAIM-482](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-482.md), and the novelty objection ([CLAIM-024](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-024.md)) against the gain claim [CLAIM-487](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-487.md), which stays Proposed. The account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

#### [SYNTHESIS-037](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-037.md): An agent made of a population of interests can act as one while they stay divided: synchronization of its interests is desirable and not necessary, the routes by which it acts as one (arbitration, a change in which interest may act, coinciding valuations, local accommodation) are distinct and differently costly, and whether its coordination switches or reorganizes continuously depends on how it is constituted

*Proposed · version 1*

A part account of the will-organization line: what makes a population of interests act as one ([QUESTION-034](../record/questions.d/QUESTION-034.md), the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11). The record's answers are Proposed: flow as valuations that do not cross ([CLAIM-162](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md)), mindfulness as a change in which interest may act ([CLAIM-156](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)), and learned local accommodation as cheaper than escalation ([CLAIM-358](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-358.md)). The owner's [CLAIM-261](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-261.md), Active, settles that acting as one does not need synchronization. Two senses of synchronization are kept apart ([TERM-050](../record/terms.d/TERM-050.md), [TERM-061](../record/terms.d/TERM-061.md)). The account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

#### [SYNTHESIS-044](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-044.md): An organization's regulatory difficulty is frustration among its maintained demands, an ordinal fact about which sets of them can be jointly met; its perspectives' activation, tolerance, claims and grants are quantities separate from that fact, so a quiet perspective need not be satisfied and raising a threshold is not relief; and motivational integration is the co-satisfaction of the demands within tolerances the will can recognize

*Proposed · version 1*

A part account of the will-organization line: frustration among an organization's demands and the quantities its perspectives carry. The owner's correction that frustration, not distress, is the primitive ([CLAIM-368](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md)) and that it is ordinal ([CLAIM-347](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)) is worked out as a compatibility complex with relief as its enlargement, then separated from realized violation ([CLAIM-357](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md)), from what keeps perspectives quiet ([CLAIM-549](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-549.md)), from activation and its tolerance ([CLAIM-548](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-548.md), [CLAIM-550](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-550.md)) and from conferral ([CLAIM-552](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-552.md)). [CLAIM-534](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-534.md) makes motivational integration co-satisfaction within recognizable tolerances. The account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CLAIM-368](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md) | CLAIM | Active | The primitive for an organization's regulatory difficulty is frustration, not distress: a relation between maintained, consequential demands and the incompatibilities, constraints or countervailing processes that limit their realization, independent of strain, the burden of sustaining activity, and distinct from distress, a possible integrated response to either |
| [CLAIM-347](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) | CLAIM | Active | Frustration among an organization's demands is an ordinal fact before it is a quantity: the jointly satisfiable sets of demands form a downward-closed complex whose minimal non-faces are the minimal conflicts, relief is strict enlargement of that complex for the same declared demands, reorganizations that relieve different conflicts are incomparable, and dropping or suppressing a demand is not relief |

| [CLAIM-500](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-500.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | The governance-induced kind of frustration is not idle: some failures of an organization's actual updates to meet demands that an admissible update would meet are explained by how influence is allocated, and not by step size, curvature, noise, conditioning or a fixed weighting rule |
| [CLAIM-554](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-554.md) | CLAIM | Active | Niche differentiation matters to an organization's development as possible relief of structural frustration among its constituents' persistence demands, a strict enlargement of their compatibility complex over viable histories for the same demands, and not as reduced competition: competition, contested rankings, structural and governance frustration, operative thwarting, strain and coexistence come apart, so lower competitive intensity, the exclusion of a constituent or a redistribution of influence relieves no structural frustration of the original demands, and specialization can relieve frustration where nothing competes |

| [CLAIM-534](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-534.md) | CLAIM | Active | A plural will's motivational integration, a dimension of freedom of will the record names and leaves unanalysed, is the extent to which the demands it maintains are jointly met, within tolerances it can recognize, across the contexts where they interact, and kept so under its own dynamics; it is neither agreement among the demands nor the dominance of one, and its parts come apart: realizability (the tolerance frontier), realization (governance frustration), maintenance (viability) and the allocation of the tolerance each demand gives up |
| [CLAIM-537](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md) | CLAIM | Active | In tolerance-bounded compatibility on a graph with disturbed offsets, \|Dx − a₀ − w\| ≤ δ for \|w_e\| ≤ η_e, a compatible configuration exists for every disturbance exactly when \|cᵀa₀\| + Σ η_e\|c_e\| ≤ Σ δ_e\|c_e\| on every cycle, and one configuration serves every disturbance exactly when η ≤ δ and \|cᵀa₀\| ≤ Σ(δ_e − η_e)\|c_e\|; an agent that chooses its configuration from what it observes needs the second condition within each class of disturbances it cannot tell apart, so whether a compatible state can be selected lies between the two and depends on what the agent can read |
| [CLAIM-628](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-628.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | In tolerance-bounded compatibility on a graph with disturbed offsets, one configuration serves every disturbance in a class the agent cannot tell apart exactly when, on each overlap, the class's half-range of disturbance is within tolerance, and the cycle condition for compatibility holds for the class's midpoint offsets with each tolerance reduced by that half-range; whether a compatible configuration exists depends on a disturbance only through its cohomology class, but whether one can be selected depends on its edgewise spread, so an agent that reads the cohomology class exactly need not be able to select one |
| [CLAIM-548](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-548.md) | CLAIM | Active | A motivational process can become active, and act, without any expectation that its response will succeed: its activation, the authority the organization grants it and the efficacy of what it does are separate quantities, so a threshold on expected net benefit is one special case of an activation threshold and not its general form |

| [CLAIM-550](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-550.md) | CLAIM | Active | A perspective's tolerance of departure from what it maintains can be derived from its activation threshold: if its activation is z = b(c) + α(c)d, rising with discrepancy d (α > 0), and it acts with probability σ(κ(z − θ)), the discrepancy it tolerates while acting with probability at most ε is (θ + κ⁻¹ logit ε − b(c))/α(c); so one fixed threshold gives different tolerances across contexts through baseline and gain, a negative tolerance marks activation driven by something other than the discrepancy, and raising a threshold enlarges tolerance without relieving any demand |
| [CLAIM-551](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-551.md) | CLAIM | Active | Read in DBT's sense, cognitive dysregulation is a consequence of emotion dysregulation, not a failure to allocate attention: a perspective with high gain, intense response and slow return to baseline has a small and lingering tolerance, can stay active when the current discrepancy no longer warrants it, and while active supplies the interpretation that governance acts on, so the effective will becomes mood-dependent; it predicts impairment that follows arousal and its slow decay, where the attentional reading predicts impairment that follows competing demand on a fixed budget |
| [CLAIM-552](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-552.md) | CLAIM | Active | A perspective's tolerance for another process's contribution is its criterion for conferring influence on that contribution, set by its own priorities: tolerances are directed, and the discrepancy each measures is the perspective's own, so inside its tolerance the perspective's interventions raise the other's share of future influence and outside it they lower it; meeting the tolerance is necessary for that conferral where the criterion binds, and sufficient only for a grant, under a rule that grants influence on it |

| [CLAIM-447](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-447.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Model-based wanting is a pursuit process's ranking of the futures it predicts under candidate interventions, P(S \| do(a)) against P(S \| do(a₀)), while cue-triggered wanting is learned salience that need not compute those futures; a process's causal model, its wanting and its practical efficacy are separable, so learning to want differently, learning that a want will not pay, and learning not to act on it are three different changes |

#### [SYNTHESIS-039](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-039.md): Maintaining an effective regime and maintaining the capacity to govern among regimes are different achievements, since stability does not entail viability: a protective regime can keep itself in place by shaping the evidence and authority that would end it, an organization can record a correction without maintaining the capacity it needs, and resolve, release and a learned prior over which processes govern are among the relations that keep or lose that capacity

*Proposed · version 1*

A part account of the will-organization line: the will paper's main result and what the record has built on it. [ARG-007](../record/arguments.d/ARG-007.md) concludes [CLAIM-099](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-099.md) from [CLAIM-079](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-079.md) and [CLAIM-025](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md): effective action and the capacity to govern among regimes are different achievements, with Canguilhem as an interpretation and not a premise ([CLAIM-018](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-018.md)). On that separation rest the separation of access, authority and action ([CLAIM-349](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md)), correction against maintained capacity ([CLAIM-422](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-422.md)), resolve ([CLAIM-344](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-344.md)) and robustness ([CLAIM-359](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-359.md)), and the Proposed accounts of release ([CLAIM-465](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-465.md)), governance-maintained anxiety ([CLAIM-446](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md)) and self-maintaining protection ([CLAIM-445](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-445.md)). Seventeen Open questions are promotion conditions moved off its readings. The account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

#### [SYNTHESIS-041](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-041.md): Freedom of will comes in degrees along separable dimensions, compared by inclusion of what an agent can viably reach, and in the operational sense the record proposes it is an agent's governance of its own governability; sensitivity and controllability fall short of it, self-formation is the production of a new distinction or channel that outlasts its occasion, and explaining efficacy does not settle whose the will is

*Proposed · version 1*

A part account of the will-organization line: freedom of will and whose the will is. The owner's [CLAIM-354](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md) makes freedom of will a profile of separable dimensions under a partial order. [CLAIM-545](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md) (Proposed, admitted by a separating case) identifies freedom, operationally, with governance of one's own governability, resting on that profile, on [CLAIM-523](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md)'s three achievements and on [CLAIM-533](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md)'s point that sensitivity is not control. [CLAIM-532](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md) says what self-formation produces. [CLAIM-022](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-022.md) disclaims ownership, and [QUESTION-071](../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md) and [QUESTION-364](../record/questions.d/QUESTION-364.md) hold manipulation and continuation open. The account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

## Normative judgment about organizations

whether an organization's own dynamics ground norms of function and failure, and what judging an organization needs beyond them — fixed relata before a judgment is well-defined, viability that does not establish what ought to persist, histories a present state does not show, and a bounded duty of answerability for the wrong beyond harm; split from will-organization ([ADR-089](../record/decisions.d/ADR-089.md))

### [SYNTHESIS-038](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md): A normative judgment about an organization is well-defined only once its relata are fixed and can then be false; viability does not establish what ought to persist; judgments of continuity, reform and obligation can need histories that a present state does not show; and the wrong beyond harm that an organization commits by reproducing what keeps a justified standard from constraining it is proposed as a breach of a bounded duty of answerability

*Proposed · version 2*

The account of the organizational-normativity line: what the record holds about normative judgment of organizations. The paper disclaims that viability establishes what ought to persist ([CLAIM-075](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md)). The owner's [CLAIM-363](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) holds that a normative judgment needs fixed relata and can then be false, and [CLAIM-518](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md), narrowed under [CLAIM-512](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-512.md)'s objection, that some judgments need histories. The owner's [CLAIM-614](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-614.md) presupposes a wrong beyond harm in an organization that reproduces what hides its harm; A's [CLAIM-624](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) (Proposed, admitted) makes it a bounded duty of answerability, and [CLAIM-619](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-619.md) a counter-corrective disposition. The account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

## Organizational affect

affective states as properties of organized systems, read through Frijda — the line the will paper grew out of

### [SYNTHESIS-021](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-021.md): The organizational-affect line is three accounts joined at the potential account of valence: what valence is in an organization, a persistent potential of its perspectives' negotiation; what affect a corporation can bear and what that does to the line between remorse and prudence; and when such a regime is felt and whose it is taken to be; the account of valence rests on the functional thesis about corporate affect, the account of feeling rests on the account of valence, and the line makes no claim beyond its parts

*Proposed · version 2*

The account of the organizational-affect line, over the accounts of its three parts: the potential account of valence and its tests ([SYNTHESIS-020](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-020.md)), corporate affect and responsibility ([SYNTHESIS-018](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-018.md)), and feeling and access ([SYNTHESIS-022](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-022.md)). They meet at [CLAIM-440](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md), which rests on [CLAIM-039](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md) and on which [CLAIM-439](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-439.md) rests. No link between the parts that the record does not state passed [ADR-075](../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s test, so the account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

| [CLAIM-440](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | An organization's appraisal is the negotiation among its perspectives, a common currency is that negotiation's admitting an ordering of the options it faces, and goal-conduciveness valence is a regime in which an ordering of the organization's own states by their bearing on its maintenance prevails in the negotiation; so valence presupposes contested rankings, not frustrated demands, its sign is whether the organization runs ahead of or behind a reference course along the potential ordering, its intensity is how far the negotiation's decisions follow that ordering, and ambivalence, where no ordering prevails, differs from neutrality, where one prevails and the organization keeps to its course |
| [CLAIM-432](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-432.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | A corporation can be an agent fit to be held responsible and the bearer of functional affect in Frijda's sense, so psychopathy's affective features can be assigned to it as well as its conduct: it lacks remorse, functionally, when harm it does to others is not among the concerns its own appraisals track and gains precedence over what it does only when a regulator or a market turns it into a threat to the corporation's concerns; that profile, threat without remorse, is the construct's, and it is changed by redesigning the corporation's concerns, not its members' characters |
| [CLAIM-355](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | In a distributed agent the binding of appraisal, readiness and governance into one response can be real while the single owner a self-model or collective self-description attributes it to is a representational construction, not a further entity; the illusion, where there is one, is in the attribution and belongs to whichever system adopts the representation, and this deflates the self without settling whether experience is real |
| [CLAIM-439](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-439.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | A regime of valence is felt, in the sense of attended and available to the system's other processes, when the system that is in it also models it: when a deeper process infers which ordering wins its negotiation, which way the system is moving along it and how strongly it prevails, and the inference is used elsewhere in the system; unfelt valence is the potential without that model, as unfelt fluency is a change in precision without the inference about it |

**What would show the account unfaithful:** A part account or component misstated or misattributed here; an in-force component of the organizational-affect line that no part account integrates; or a link stated here that neither a part account nor a component states.

## Authenticity and concordance

what makes a will-organization the agent's own, and normativity across the scales an agent spans. Set aside on 2026-10-05 as future work

### [SYNTHESIS-023](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-023.md): The authenticity line holds, set aside, that a will is the agent's own to the degree its commitments arise through, remain integrated with and are answerable to its constitutive organization, and that this grounds normativity from a whole to its constituents but not between peers; it was deferred because its ownership criteria do not survive manipulation, and what it has gained since is a candidate content for "integrated", non-domination of the processes that carry a commitment, with the objection that non-domination cannot be read from low supervisory cost, or from override alone, but only under intervention, when a constituent dissents, or from history

*Proposed · version 1*

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CLAIM-016](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-016.md) | CLAIM | Deferred | An organized agent's will is its own to the degree that its operative commitments arise through, remain integrated with, and are answerable to its constitutive organization |
| [CLAIM-096](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-096.md) | CLAIM | Deferred | Where several agents share an environment, the realization of one agent's will changes the conditions under which others can realize theirs, and that interaction is itself a normative object |
| [CLAIM-104](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-104.md) | CLAIM | Deferred | Authenticity grounds normativity downward, from an encompassing agent to its constituents, but not across agents at one level |
| [CLAIM-362](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-362.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Non-domination of an agent's subcomponents is a candidate constituent of authenticity as an organizational achievement, not a sufficient criterion of ownership: higher-level processes need not impose the outcome because the lower-level ones already support it or settle their disagreement among themselves, and a process that rarely decides keeps access to the roles in which it is consequential |
| [CLAIM-364](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-364.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Processes conditioned never to object coordinate without override at the same behaviour and supervisory cost as processes that negotiate, so the two part only under intervention, when a constituent dissents, or in their history |
| [ARG-030](../record/arguments.d/ARG-030.md) | ARG | Proposed | Low supervisory cost shows that an organization does not dominate its processes |
| [CASE-128](../record/cases.d/CASE-128.md) | CASE | Active | The voluntary delegation: a person gives a friend the password to a distracting application during a calm period and is refused it later under temptation, while another person lives under the same restriction imposed without consent |
| [CASE-129](../record/cases.d/CASE-129.md) | CASE | Active | The alarm that learned and the alarm that was disabled: two systems that once warned too often are both quiet in ordinary operation, and only one responds when a new hazard appears |

**What would show the account unfaithful:** A component misstated or misattributed here, its voice or status included; an in-force component whose line is authenticity left out without a reason given; or a link this account states that no component states. Its standing is its components': most of them are Deferred with the line, and a component retired, demoted or reopened takes its clause with it, and nothing here holds the clause up.

## Nucleating an argument

how an argument developed across stateless sessions settles into stable, addressable structure — what drifts, what anchors it, and what anchoring costs. What a record of it keeps, and the record as its own apparatus, are lines of their own ([ADR-082](../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md))

### [SYNTHESIS-016](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-016.md): The nucleating-argument line is three accounts that meet at the rule for when to code an argument: what fails when an argument is restated, how coding at the second occurrence stops it, and when filing pays; the one claim the line makes beyond its parts is that the rule's drift-catching and cost-competitive justifications part when filing is dear

*Proposed · version 3*

The account of the nucleating-argument line, over the accounts of its three parts: drift ([SYNTHESIS-014](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-014.md)), anchors ([SYNTHESIS-013](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-013.md)) and the costs of anchoring ([SYNTHESIS-015](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-015.md)). They meet at [ADR-032](../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)'s rule for when to code an argument, which the anchors part justifies by drift ([CLAIM-176](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md)) and the costs part by effort ([CLAIM-308](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md)). Where the two justifications part is [CLAIM-630](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-630.md)'s, a derivation in the assistant's voice. The account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CLAIM-630](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-630.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Where filing an argument costs at least twice what one reconstruction overpays, the break-even filing rule files it later than its second occurrence, and every reconstruction it pays for in between is a restatement with nothing filed to check it against: the cost-competitive rule and the drift-catching second-occurrence rule part exactly when filing is that dear, and the competitive guarantee prices none of the drift between them |
| [CLAIM-176](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Recurrence is the trigger of persistence this record is built around: coding a thing the second time it turns up captures exactly the drift that defeats an argument, and keeps capture from flooding the record |
| [CLAIM-177](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) | CLAIM | Active | In the record's exchanges with collaborators who keep no memory, the argument repeatedly loses identity: concepts are redefined silently, objections and readings come back as though new, and the thesis changes without anyone arguing for the change |
| [CLAIM-185](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | The nucleation threshold of an argument is whatever makes a structure persist: a persistent structure is available as an anchor, and more complex structure can evolve only on anchors |
| [CLAIM-186](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | How fast an argument grows sets how it grows: drift tracks how fast new material arrives relative to how fast it is anchored, so a fast, prolific exchange branches, as a crystal grown far from equilibrium does, and a project memory stabilizes an argument by keeping anchoring up with arrival |
| [CLAIM-303](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Filing an argument moves work across time: it is paid for now, in filing, indexing, tracking dependencies and checking it is still current, against reconstruction later, so it is worth its cost only when expected reuse covers it, and recurrence is evidence of reuse, not the criterion |
| [CLAIM-308](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Where reuse cannot be forecast, recurrence weighted by reconstruction cost is the filing criterion, not only evidence for one: filing at the first use at which reconstructing again would take the overpayment past the cost of filing is within 2 − (c_a + u)/c_r of the hindsight optimum on every sequence of uses, at most twice, and no deterministic rule without foresight guarantees materially better, under fixed known costs, with staleness left out and the cost of recognizing what a filed argument answers taken as fixed |

**What would show the account unfaithful:** A part account or component misstated or misattributed here; an in-force component of the line that no part account integrates; or a link stated here that neither a part account, a component nor [CLAIM-630](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-630.md) states.

#### [SYNTHESIS-015](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-015.md): Anchoring has costs and a price: an early anchor can entrench its framing, and iterative retrieval can turn a framing into a premise, though adaptive search is not biased in itself; filing moves work across time and pays only when reuse covers it, recurrence weighted by reconstruction cost is a worst-case guarantee where reuse cannot be forecast, and recognizing what a filed argument answers has a cost that grows with what is stored

| [CLAIM-301](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-301.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Iterative retrieval can turn a provisional interpretation into a premise: a framing selects what is encountered, what is encountered reinforces the framing, and the question being investigated drifts as well as the queries |
| [CLAIM-292](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-292.md) | CLAIM | Active | Retrieval that depends on current belief is not a bias in itself: adaptive search can be rational when inference accounts for how the evidence was selected, and calling a search biased needs a standard outside the search |

## What a record of inquiry keeps

what a record of a developing argument or inquiry can secure through revision — traceable change, accountability structure, decision sufficiency — and what keeping it buys beyond current conclusions; split from nucleating-argument ([ADR-082](../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md))

### [SYNTHESIS-017](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-017.md): What a record of a developing argument can secure is traceable change over its accountability structure, which is neither sufficiency for revision nor correctness: current conclusions and support topology do not fix revisions, a sufficient state makes history redundant only while its model and decisions hold, and what kept justifications can buy is a wider family of decisions and decisions a bounded agent could not otherwise make

| [CLAIM-181](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | The record fixes the grammar an argument is expressed in, though not its shape: its closed vocabulary of schemes, roles and relations formalizes early, and a move that fits no CLAIM, TERM, ARG or declared relation is forced into one or lost until the misfit is noticed and the grammar amended to hold it |
| [CLAIM-189](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Fidelity is the wrong measure of a developing argument: maturing drops and changes things legitimately, so what a record can secure is traceability, change that is announced and located, not preservation |
| [CLAIM-250](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | What a developing argument should preserve through legitimate revision is its accountability structure, what was asserted, why, how it was challenged and what justified its revision, not its propositions, so fidelity is defined over justificatory and provenance relations while propositional content changes |
| [CLAIM-293](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md) | CLAIM | Active | The topology of a support graph does not fix how a conclusion should be revised when one of its supports fails: two records with the same edges can carry evidence of different strength and call for different revisions |

## The record as its own apparatus

what an apparatus of record-keeping makes determinate, how its grammar is fixed and revised through use, and inquiry as specification — the record itself as the case; split from nucleating-argument ([ADR-082](../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md))

### [SYNTHESIS-012](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-012.md): The record's grammar is an apparatus in the operational sense: fixed at any moment, amended by decision when a misfit is noticed, and made of typed relations more rigid than their relata without being sound for it; that it constitutes the record's objects is Proposed; and its revision is the record's own case of inquiry as specification, an inquiry that can revise what an answer could be and specifies under resource bounds

*Proposed · version 1*

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CLAIM-181](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | The record fixes the grammar an argument is expressed in, though not its shape: its closed vocabulary of schemes, roles and relations formalizes early, and a move that fits no CLAIM, TERM, ARG or declared relation is forced into one or lost until the misfit is noticed and the grammar amended to hold it |
| [CLAIM-183](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-183.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Generated views of the record, fed back into the exchange, become instruments of the argument: they show where its terms evolved faster than its formalism |
| [CLAIM-419](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md) | CLAIM | Active | The record's grammar is fixed at any moment but amendable by decision, and in practice a move that fit no scheme or relation has repeatedly been treated as a defect of the grammar and answered by amending it, so a move the grammar cannot hold is not only forced or lost; whether every such move is caught is not shown |
| [CLAIM-469](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-469.md) | CLAIM | Active | Luria is an apparatus for a record's objects in the operational sense: through its schemes, vocabularies, validators and generated views it realizes a system of distinctions that fixes what counts as a referable and governable object within the record, so that a split scheme makes one object two and a promoted vocabulary makes a value an entity; it keeps, enforces and propagates those distinctions; and its distinctions are revised through the record's own use |
| [CLAIM-470](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-470.md) | CLAIM | Active | Inquiry is a form of specification: a question fixes which differences would count as an answer, an inquiry adds the operations that make those differences accessible, and what it finds can stabilize into a specification that constrains later inquiry; so inquiry stands to its findings as a specification to its realizations, with one difference, that an inquiry can revise what an answer could be |
| [CLAIM-472](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-472.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Because an apparatus makes some distinctions determinate and leaves others unstatable, choosing and maintaining one is open to evaluation and not only to verification; but that a cut excludes something fixes no obligation, since every distinction excludes, and which exclusions matter is a judgment indexed to a standard, a scale and those affected |
| [CLAIM-475](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md) | CLAIM | Active | Specifying is itself a resource-bounded realization: formulating a question takes time, concepts and computation as realizing a configuration takes energy and matter, so the questions an agent can ask are a product of what it has already realized; a stabilized specification is past inquiry stored so that later questions become cheaper to ask, and it can make other questions harder |
| [CLAIM-476](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Beyond what it does operationally, luria is an apparatus in Barad's constitutive sense for the objects of a record, and only for them: the record's objects are constituted, and not only made referable and governable, by the distinctions its grammar enacts, so that the same authored material is a different set of objects under a revised apparatus, and the record's own inquiry reconstitutes the apparatus that constitutes them |
| [CLAIM-479](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-479.md) | CLAIM | Active | In the record a typed relation is more constrained than either of its relata: a claim's content is open prose, while `rests_on` fixes the scheme at both ends, has `supports` written as its converse and says what retiring its target leaves, and none of that moves when either claim's content does; so a relation's rigidity is a fact about the grammar, not evidence that the dependency it records is sound |
| [CASE-131](../record/cases.d/CASE-131.md) | CASE | Active | The graph that asserted an inference nobody made: filing one claim as supporting another made the record's link fixer write that the other rested on it, and the record answered by adding a relation |
| [CASE-178](../record/cases.d/CASE-178.md) | CASE | Active | How the record's grammar grows: after its scaffold, this record filed documents on all 32 days, added vocabulary terms on 18, fields or relations to schemes on 8, whole vocabularies on 3, schemes on 1 and a remote project on 1, so the owner's ordering of levels holds by frequency; but each refinement came in the same pull request as the documents that needed it and, nine times in ten, an ADR, so the levels are rarer events of one loop of work, not slower processes of their own, and the grammar's rates fell while filing rose |
| [CASE-180](../record/cases.d/CASE-180.md) | CASE | Active | The record's own rates: over its first fifty days, measured from git, an entry's prose is revised about once in 22 days once drafting is over, its status once in 128, an authored relation gained or lost once in 132 and an authored relation retracted once in about 600, while no relation type has been redeclared; the layers' event rates are ordered as the exchange guessed, but only after the first day, when all of them change together, and the grammar is slow to revise without being slow to grow |

## Evidence for experience

what could show that a system, organized, non-biological or without a cortex, has experience and not only access or function, and what each kind of evidence (report, deficit, architecture, behaviour) can and cannot establish

### [SYNTHESIS-019](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-019.md): The owner's thesis that experience is constituted by interpretive organization stands with its sufficiency condition unstated: interpretation as such does not suffice, current grounding and a represented owner are kept apart from what would make an organization experiential, the line's one candidate condition makes valence felt only in the access sense, and each test of the rest meets the limit that the record's evidence about experience reaches it through access

| [CLAIM-411](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md) | CLAIM | Active | Under the broad, nonphenomenal definition of interpretation the constitutive thesis uses, substantial processing that is not independently shown to be experiential meets the definition, blindsight's apparently unconscious visual discrimination among it, so interpretation alone does not establish experience, and the thesis must say which further organizational properties, if any, make an interpretation experiential |
| [CLAIM-412](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Experience is constituted by interpretive organization, not produced by it: an appropriately organized process in which signals acquire significance for a system is the experience, so whether a system can have experience becomes whether it can sustain that organization |
| [CLAIM-413](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-413.md) | CLAIM | Active | Grounding is not a property of an experience but a relation among an interpretation, what it purports to be about, and a process that constrains it independently; its current, developmental and epistemic senses come apart from one another, and in the current sense it comes apart from whether the interpretation occurs, so ungrounded is not unconstrained, and what makes an interpretive organization experiential need not be what makes its contents veridical |
| [CLAIM-414](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md) | CLAIM | Active | Matched ordinary trajectories can conceal differences in an interpretation's efficacy, in the allocation of that efficacy, and in the maintenance of its enabling constraints: in two finite constructions, systems that agree under ordinary operation differ in each, and a specified intervention exposes the difference that passive observation of the matched trajectories does not |
| [CLAIM-439](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-439.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | A regime of valence is felt, in the sense of attended and available to the system's other processes, when the system that is in it also models it: when a deeper process infers which ordering wins its negotiation, which way the system is moving along it and how strongly it prevails, and the inference is used elsewhere in the system; unfelt valence is the potential without that model, as unfelt fluency is a change in precision without the inference about it |

## How training finds structure

why trained networks come to have the structure they have, which features, symmetries and connected solution sets training reaches and why — understanding, not instruction for practice, which belongs to the anthology

### [SYNTHESIS-030](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-030.md): The learned-structure line is several inquiries into what training reaches that barely relate: whether a learner's demands are frustrated and whose they are, when structure is acquired, whether optimal representations nest, whether trained solutions are connected, when a learned distinction is a concept, and what classification leaves in the last layers, with smaller families on personas, group structure and learned variables and twenty-three entries linked to no other; the parts meet almost only through two questions on acquisition, and the line is a candidate to split

#### [SYNTHESIS-026](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-026.md): Whether a learner's demands share a descent direction is decided by a test that a change of chart, or a function-preserving symmetry that is a diffeomorphism, leaves unchanged, while gradient cosines and a residual budgeted in a fixed Euclidean norm can change; the compatibility complex of the demands and the singular geometry of learning are invariants of one object; and in conventional training the demands, and any condition they put the learner in, belong to the optimizer–model–data system rather than to the network

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|

| [CLAIM-629](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-629.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Whether several objectives share a strict first-order descent direction is constant on the orbits of any function-preserving symmetry that acts on the parameters as a diffeomorphism, so permutation, positive rescaling across a ReLU and orthogonal maps of a residual stream all leave the verdict unchanged; a frustration residual budgeted in a fixed Euclidean norm is constant on an orbit only where the symmetry's derivative is orthogonal, so it holds across permutations and orthogonal maps and changes along rescalings |
| [CLAIM-555](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-555.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | In statistical learning, the compatibility complex of the demands a training distribution presents and the singular geometry singular learning theory studies are two invariants of one object, not descriptions of two: each demand's acceptance set is a sublevel set of its loss on the parameter space, the complex is the nerve of those sets, and the aggregate loss whose geometry fixes the learning coefficient is built from the same losses; the nerve is coarse, the learning coefficient finer, and over a fixed architecture the complex changes in training only through which configurations are accessible |
| [CLAIM-263](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-263.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Whether two trained networks compute the same way can be tested by quotienting the architecture's full symmetry group and measuring what remains: a barrier that survives alignment marks a different mechanism, connection after alignment means shared feature structure, and the test cannot run where features have no counterpart |

## Readiness and slack

what it takes to keep, reach and pay for capacities whose value lies in rare circumstances — readiness as response capability, slack and reconfiguration slack as different reserves, the resource threshold of a transition and its obstructions, and budget rules that remove options no one chose to give up ([ADR-073](../record/decisions.d/ADR-073.md)). When transient support can be withdrawn is a line of its own ([ADR-087](../record/decisions.d/ADR-087.md))

### [SYNTHESIS-031](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-031.md): The readiness line is two accounts, of keeping a rare capability and judging its worth and of reaching and paying for configurations under budgets, which meet at budget rules, slack and what a reserve costs; they are closed by relations and joined by mentions, and no link between them that no part states passes the claim test; when transient support can be withdrawn, once a third part, is a line of its own

*Proposed · version 2*

The account of the readiness line, over the accounts of its two parts: keeping and judging a rare capability ([SYNTHESIS-027](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-027.md)) and reaching and paying for configurations ([SYNTHESIS-024](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-024.md)). They meet at budget rules and slack ([CASE-200](../record/cases.d/CASE-200.md), [CLAIM-577](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-577.md), [QUESTION-386](../record/questions.d/QUESTION-386.md)) and at what a reserve costs ([CLAIM-569](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-569.md)). [CLAIM-602](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md), which moved to transient-support at the split, keeps readiness because it bears on [QUESTION-386](../record/questions.d/QUESTION-386.md), and is integrated here. The account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CLAIM-602](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) | CLAIM | Active | Where an organization's capacity is learned by doing the work it serves, and decays with disuse, outside supply that does the work first lowers the capacity kept, and the longer it does all of it the longer recovery takes once it stops, while supply that covers only what the organization cannot yet do leaves its learning untouched, so what decides dependence is the order in which supply and capacity are used, not the amount of supply |

**What would show the account unfaithful:** A part account or component misstated or misattributed here; an in-force component of the readiness line that neither a part account nor this account integrates; or a link between the parts, or across to transient-support, stated here that no part account and no component states.

#### [SYNTHESIS-024](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-024.md): Reaching a configuration has a resource threshold of its own, the least peak over admissible paths, which can exceed what holding either end takes and is relative to a fixed architecture; feasible, reachable and reliably reached come apart, failures of a transition have distinct remedies, a form needs separate resources to build, keep and move, several resources give a non-convex frontier rather than a total, and a budget set to last period's spending loses every transition that needs slack with no sign in output

| [CLAIM-567](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-567.md) | CLAIM | Active | That a target configuration is feasible, that it is reachable from the start under the admissible transformations, and that the process reliably reaches it are three properties, each implied by the next and none implying it |

## Withdrawing transient support

when support that establishes or sustains a party can be withdrawn without its decline — supplied upkeep that never becomes optional, supply that does the party's work and lowers the capacity it keeps, a savings buffer as a stock of time, dependency against division of labour by who supplies, and independence from what founded an organization against independence from what feeds it; split from readiness ([ADR-087](../record/decisions.d/ADR-087.md))

### [SYNTHESIS-032](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-032.md): Transient support can be withdrawn safely only under conditions the record states jointly in one claim: supply that does the upkeep never becomes optional, supply that does the party's work lowers the capacity it keeps and, where capacity is needed to grow capacity, has a deadline after which withdrawal does not restore it, a savings buffer is a stock of time, and a capability lost to reliable supply is dependency or division of labour by who supplies it; most of the line's questions are replications of the readings it rests on

*Proposed · version 5*

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| [QUESTION-399](../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md) | QUESTION | Open | Under what conditions does a productive partial organization become a self-maintaining nucleus, one whose continued operation contributes to regenerating the very constraints that make its productive influence possible? |
| [CLAIM-606](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | A localized structure can persist by an internal balance that needs no supply, by a balance of gain and loss that needs a standing supply, or by a topological charge that continuous change cannot remove, and the three differ in what carries the structure's identity, how it forms and how it ends; because thresholds and abrupt ends appear in all of them, even with no supply at all, only withdrawing the supply and measuring the outflow tells which route a structure is on |
| [CLAIM-604](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md) | CLAIM | Active | Where each damaged part of a structure is repaired by drawing on a flux at a rate proportional to the structure's intact share, as a flame's upkeep is, it has an ignition threshold below which it goes out with the supply still on, a supply level below which it collapses rather than declines, and an outage after which restoring the supply does not relight it; repair supplied at a rate set by the supply alone, whatever the structure's state, has none of the three |
| [CLAIM-597](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) | CLAIM | Active | Where every replacement part is supplied from outside, an organization can become independent of what founded it but never of what feeds it: with damage at rate d and supplied repair at rate ρs the intact fraction holds at ρs/(ρs + d), needs a supply growing as θ/(1 − θ) times the damage rate to hold a share θ, and decays as e^(−dt) once the supply stops, as DNA origami that self-heals from a strand pool and origami that replicates from supplied monomers both illustrate |
| [CLAIM-602](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) | CLAIM | Active | Where an organization's capacity is learned by doing the work it serves, and decays with disuse, outside supply that does the work first lowers the capacity kept, and the longer it does all of it the longer recovery takes once it stops, while supply that covers only what the organization cannot yet do leaves its learning untouched, so what decides dependence is the order in which supply and capacity are used, not the amount of supply |
| [CLAIM-605](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md) | CLAIM | Active | Where capacity is learned by doing, decays with disuse and needs capacity already present to grow, support that does the work has a deadline after which withdrawal no longer restores capacity, and a slow taper of such support is worse than an abrupt cut because it holds practice down long enough to cross the threshold; support that covers only what the party cannot yet do needs no taper but cannot lift a party already below the threshold |
| [CLAIM-601](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md) | CLAIM | Active | A savings buffer is a stock of time: where shocks must be absorbed or a household is ruined, an investment that pays only after a delay is worth taking only above a buffer that rises with the delay, so households with the same preferences decline profitable delayed investments below it, a choice that reads as impatience and is the right policy for survival by a deadline; covering needs through the delay buys the time |
| [CLAIM-603](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity |
| [CLAIM-600](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) | CLAIM | Active | Transient support can be withdrawn safely only if it started a process that keeps itself going on a flux that will stay available, was large enough to carry the supported party past any threshold that process has, outlasted the threat it stood in for, and left the work to the party throughout, in each subtask it must later do alone and not only in its role as a whole, at no more effort than it could bear, and, where the capacity is cumulative and its field moves fast, kept up after withdrawal; inputs the party cannot produce must stay supplied as a standing part of the arrangement; support that fails these leaves dependence or decay, but meeting them all is not enough, since support can carry a function nobody names before withdrawal; and persistence after withdrawal is needed to tell which, though slow reversion can mimic it |

**What would show the account unfaithful:** A component misstated or misattributed here; an in-force component of the transient-support line left out without a reason given; or a link this account states that no component states. Its standing is its components': a component retired or demoted takes its clause with it, and nothing here holds the clause up.

## Resource-bounded realizability and individuation

what a constrained system can realize, reach, tell apart and become under computational and physical bounds — compatibility against reachability, budgeted composition of processes, finding against navigating, restricted and enriched Yoneda profiles, isomorphism against persistence, with origami as the laboratory ([ADR-073](../record/decisions.d/ADR-073.md))

### [SYNTHESIS-043](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-043.md): The realizability line is four accounts, of reaching under resources, of budgeted individuation, of assembly and productive nucleation, and of persisting organized individuals, which meet at the separation of assembling, persisting and regenerating a form; the first three are densely joined, the persistence part points out and receives nothing, and no link between the parts that no part states passes the claim test

*Proposed · version 1*

The account of the realizability line, over the accounts of its four parts: reaching under resources ([SYNTHESIS-042](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-042.md)), budgeted individuation ([SYNTHESIS-040](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-040.md)), assembly and productive nucleation ([SYNTHESIS-045](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-045.md)) and persisting organized individuals ([SYNTHESIS-046](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-046.md)). [CLAIM-566](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-566.md), A's separation of assembling, persisting and regenerating a form, is linked from every part and is integrated here directly. The first three parts are densely joined; [SYNTHESIS-046](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-046.md)'s stored relations all point out of it. The withdrawal inquiry, once part of this line, has left it for transient-support ([ADR-087](../record/decisions.d/ADR-087.md), [ADR-088](../record/decisions.d/ADR-088.md)). The account adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'.

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CLAIM-566](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-566.md) | CLAIM | Active | That a form assembles, that it persists over a specified horizon and that the system regenerates it after turnover are three properties with separate probabilities, and a structure that assembles and persists without producing the constraints that would regenerate it does not show organizational closure |

**What would show the account unfaithful:** A part account or component misstated or misattributed here; an in-force component of the realizability line that neither a part account nor this account integrates; or a link between the parts stated here that no part account and no component states.

#### [SYNTHESIS-042](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-042.md): What a constrained system can reach under a budget is not what it can hold: feasible, reachable and reliably reached come apart, the threshold for a transition is the least peak over admissible paths and can be infinite, a budget enlarges compatibility and reachability only up to what a fixed architecture admits and neither filtration fixes the other, failed transitions sort into obstructions with their own repairs and telling which holds can be hard, an added constraint can improve reliability and never reach, and where an intervention acts can matter more than how much

*Proposed · version 1*

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CLAIM-571](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md) | CLAIM | Active | For a fixed architecture and one resource that must be held at each moment, the resource threshold for reaching a target configuration need not equal the resource requirement of the target: it is the least, over admissible transition paths, of the peak requirement along the path, and it is infinite when no admissible path joins the two |
| [CLAIM-567](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-567.md) | CLAIM | Active | That a target configuration is feasible, that it is reachable from the start under the admissible transformations, and that the process reliably reaches it are three properties, each implied by the next and none implying it |
| [CLAIM-568](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-568.md) | CLAIM | Active | A transition can fail in four ways that call for different remedies: a feasible path exceeds a resource ceiling, no path exists in the fixed configuration space, a path exists that no available input can execute, or a path exists that cannot be reliably followed; added actuation can overcome an energy barrier and cannot join disconnected configurations |
| [CLAIM-556](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-556.md) | CLAIM | Active | Before the four obstructions to a transition stands a failure of compatibility, no configuration meeting the demands, repaired by changing the constraints, since dropping a demand is not relief; and after them a failure of regeneration, the capability not surviving turnover, repaired by maintenance or reproduction; so a diagnosis runs through six levels, each with its own repair |
| [CLAIM-569](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-569.md) | CLAIM | Active | A form has at least three resource requirements, to construct it, to maintain it, and to move into or out of it, and none fixes another: a capability can be cheap to keep and dear to acquire, so having enough to sustain it is not having enough to acquire it |

| [CLAIM-563](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-563.md) | CLAIM | Active | When process costs compose by a monotone operation, the processes costing at most b are closed under composition whenever b composed with itself is at most b, and not otherwise once two composable processes each cost b: at every budget for a peak capacity composed by maximum, and for a cumulative expenditure composed by sum only at budgets 0 and infinity |
| [CLAIM-586](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-586.md) | CLAIM | Active | Indexing the compatibility complex by a resource budget gives a complex that grows with the budget and never exceeds the complex with no budget, so a set of demands outside the unbudgeted complex is structurally frustrated at every budget, and one inside it but outside the complex at budget b is frustrated only relative to b, short of resources and not structurally frustrated |
| [CLAIM-564](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-564.md) | CLAIM | Active | Restricting the demand–configuration Galois connection to the configurations affordable at a budget gives implications among demands that are antitone in the budget: an implication valid at a budget is valid at every lower one, so as the budget rises the compatibility complex grows and the valid implications shrink, and a set of demands no affordable configuration meets implies every demand |

#### [SYNTHESIS-040](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-040.md): A system's budgeted individuation is indexed by two budgets that run in opposite directions, observing splitting what can be told apart and acting under peak costs merging what can be turned into one another, so the two partitions agree only on levels common to both chains, which the order of probe costs decides; which category and enrichment is chosen fixes what counts as the same, and neither isomorphism nor a profile settles persistence

*Proposed · version 1*

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |

| [CLAIM-574](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-574.md) | CLAIM | Active | Distinctions drawn by restricted Yoneda profiles only grow as nested probe families grow: a natural isomorphism of profiles on a probe subcategory restricts to one on every subcategory of it, so objects equivalent under a larger family are equivalent under each smaller one and objects told apart at a lower budget stay apart at every higher one; an equivalence a richer regime breaks was relative to its regime, not false; and the monotonicity needs an every-probe comparison, which an averaged distortion is not |

#### [SYNTHESIS-045](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-045.md): Whether an assembly reaches its target is not fixed by how much resource it has: a resource that also sets the costs it pays, as heat does, gives a window and lets a schedule beat every level, abundance helps or hurts by whether the competing steps consume it, persistence and productivity vary independently, yields cannot tell a generative nucleus from a head start, and productive nucleating sets need not be closed upward; a productive nucleus is defined by what its establishment does to later formation against a declared target, comparator and horizon

*Proposed · version 1*

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |

| [CASE-216](../record/cases.d/CASE-216.md) | CASE | Active | A four-state annealing toy, unfolded, nucleus, folded and a misfold trap, with free energies and transition states linear in temperature: the fraction folded at one hour peaks at 90.4 % at 318.6 K among constant temperatures, at sixteen hours it is at least 90 % from 313 to 323.5 K, and five minutes at 327 K followed by 318 K leaves 98.5 % folded at the hour, which no constant temperature does; the chance of having reached the folded state agrees to four places |
| [CLAIM-598](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-598.md) | CLAIM | Active | Whether more of every resource raises, leaves or lowers the chance that an assembly reaches its target depends, at each branch point, on whether the competing steps consume further resource: a branch whose steps all consume alike is unchanged by uniform abundance, and one where the wrong step consumes and the right one does not is made worse by it, as Majikes et al. report for a single DNA origami fold that excess staples block |
| [CASE-217](../record/cases.d/CASE-217.md) | CASE | Active | A four-state branching model of assembly, unassembled, productive nucleus, trap and folded, in which three designs with the same target yield 59.3, 76.2 and 29.6 %, and scaling every supply by the same factor leaves the yield unchanged only while the competing exits from each state have the same molecularity |

| [TERM-117](../record/terms.d/TERM-117.md) | TERM | Active | productive nucleus: a partial organization whose establishment, relative to a declared target, context, horizon and comparator, causally improves the probability, timeliness, robustness or resource-feasible accessibility of forming the target by changing later interaction opportunities, constraints or transition rates; distinct from a structural seed and a kinetic nucleus |

#### [SYNTHESIS-046](../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-046.md): An organized individual that persists through changes of mode persists, on the record's proposed account, as the particular organization that keeps its repertoire realizable, inside it or outside it, and its identity over time as the causal transmission of that organization; locally realizable histories need not glue, and a coherent history can be terminal; and synchronization phenomena are offered as a laboratory that separates dependence and suppression by withdrawal, though a drive fixes where control lies and not whether it is coercive

*Proposed · version 1*

| component | kind | its status | what it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CLAIM-611](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-611.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | When an organized individual persists through changes of state and mode, in the dynamical and historical senses of persistence, what persists is the particular organization that keeps its repertoire realizable, not the repertoire it keeps, nor any state, mode or boundary; that organization may lie inside the individual or outside it |
| [CLAIM-615](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-615.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | An organized individual's identity over time is carried by the causal transmission of the relations that keep its repertoire realizable, not by its constituents or by any structure invariant across its realizations, so a structuralism about individuals has to be historical: the structure can change under maps that are not isomorphisms while the individual continues, two structurally identical copies can be two individuals, the transmitting organization may lie outside the individual, and when those relations part at a succession, different successors can continue different respects of it |
| [CLAIM-625](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-625.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Over time intervals, gluing and continuation are different properties of histories: under local dynamics and a pointwise viability constraint the viable histories form a sheaf, yet restriction from a longer interval to a shorter need not be onto, and a viable history on [0, t] extends viably to [0, T] exactly when its endpoint can stay viable for the remaining time, so a coherent history can be terminal |
| [CLAIM-623](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-623.md) | CLAIM | Proposed | Forgetting a hidden mechanism can turn a sheaf of histories into a presheaf of realizable observations that is not a sheaf: when the union of two overlapping intervals is itself an observable context, two observed histories can each be realizable and agree on their overlap with no realization of their union, so a gluing failure need not show a disagreement on an overlap or a cycle of three contexts |
| [ARG-074](../record/arguments.d/ARG-074.md) | ARG | Proposed | A hidden mode fixed for a run, whose observations over two overlapping periods agree on the overlap and do not paste into a realizable history, shows that a presheaf of realizable observations can fail to glue |
| [QUESTION-379](../record/questions.d/QUESTION-379.md) | QUESTION | Open | When does a coherent family of local observations and constrained interactions correspond to an object the system can construct or sustain, that is, when is such a presheaf representable in a category of realizable systems, and when it is, is the object constructible within the available resources? |
| [QUESTION-437](../record/questions.d/QUESTION-437.md) | QUESTION | Open | When locally realizable histories of a reduced variable have no common realization in the full system, does the failure identify a capacity or constraint the reduction omitted, and can it be told apart from modelling error or from observations of different systems? |
